messages.subject: problem in plotDensity
parts:
Hello,
I have had a strange experience in plotDensity. I have data that has
been BG corrected and quantile normalized and when I call plotDensity on
the arrays I don't get a single distribution(!).

More specifically, I am working with a custom cdf and trying to spot
check both the arrays and the cdf. I have run the following
preprocessing code:

chipType<-"hjay"
projectname<-"BRCA,2007"
outdir<-"epurdom/BRCA_2007" #"BRCA_2007"
cdfHjay<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)
myinitials<-"ep"
csBRCAJunct <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name=projectname,
chipType=chipType)
#background correction:
bcBRCAJunct <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(csBRCAJunct,tag=c("*",myinitials))
csBCBRCAJunct <- process(bcBRCAJunct,verbose=verbose)
#quantile normalization:
qnBRCAJunct <- QuantileNormalization(csBCBRCAJunct,
typesToUpdate="pm",tags=c("*",myinitials))
csNBRCAJunct <- process(qnBRCAJunct, verbose=verbose,force=F)
plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,col="black")

I don't get any errors currently or any message that there was an
interruption.

But curiously, when I ran this in batch mode, I got the following error
from plotDensity:

> plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,col="black")
Error in apply.default(mat, 2, density, na.rm = na.rm) :
dim(X) must have a positive length
Calls: plotDensity -> apply -> apply.default
Execution halted

However, when I go in and try again (but not redoing the preprocessing
steps) I can't replicate the error, so I can't give any further insights
into this aspect of the problem without rerunning everything, which I
think I will probably have to do since I'm having doubts.

I've attached the result from plotDensity. The only thing I can think of
is that the custom cdfs have incorrect information that is making the
program misidentify the pm versus mm. But currently the cdf is made so
that every probe in the cdf is hard-coded to have pbase=A and tbase=T,
which seems correct to me so that all of the probes should be pm. The
picture looks like the low intensity ones are correct and the high
intensity are not, which could imply interruption; but since they are
adjusted array by array and not probe by probe, that also doesn't make
sense.

Thanks,
Elizabeth

Any suggestions? I would really like to track down the source of both
problems, because as I mentioned I'm trying to double check that certain
custom cdfs are working, so any errors could be related to that.
Best,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] problem in plotDensity
parts:
Hi,

I still haven't looked at the main problem here, but I think I've
located what cause the error you get you run the code in "batch mode".
In you script, see if it helps to explicitly first load the 'affy'
package and then 'aroma.affymetrix', e.g.

library(affy);
library(aroma.affymetrix);

Here are the details. So this is error you report:

> > plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,col="black")
> Error in apply.default(mat, 2, density, na.rm = na.rm) :
> dim(X) must have a positive length
> Calls: plotDensity -> apply -> apply.default
> Execution halted

The call trace didn't make sense to me when I look at the
plotDensity() implementation(s), and the argument 'mat' and the
unnamed '2' didn't look like my code (e.g. I always write MARGIN=2),
so I my guess was that something else was sneaking in. If you go to
http://www.google.com/codesearch and search for:

"lang:r apply mat density"

your first hit is on "affy/R/plot.density.R". It turns out that the
'affy' packages implements a plotDensity() function as well, and it
has the line:

x.density <- apply(mat, 2, density)

Indeed, if you call affy::plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct) you get the same error:

Error in apply.default(mat, 2, density, na.rm = na.rm) :
dim(X) must have a positive length

It seems to me that the method dispatch is not taking place. This is
because the 'affy' package comes before aroma.light on the search path
and the latter set up a generic function whereas affy doesn't. If you
load the package 'affy' and then 'aroma.light' the latter comes before
on the search path and you don't have the problem.

There is code in aroma.affymetrix than makes sure that search path is
reordered such that 'affy' comes after aroma.affymetrix, but this also
show that it should come after aroma.light. [Yes, namespaces solve
part of these problems, but adds others...]. I'll try to fix this in
the next release.

So, one out of two issues solved, I hope.

Cheers

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: problem in plotDensity
parts:
Hi Henrik,

Thanks that solved the first problem (the error in batch mode) --
interestingly it was not always a problem because I could do plotDensity
for my raw data in batch mode but not for my normalized data. But
regardless, plotDensity now runs fine.

However, I'm still getting not exactly the same distribution for all the
quantile normalized arrays when I plot (I've done this for other
experiments/cdfs and it is *exactly* the same). I have started clean by
deleting all but the raw cel files and deleting the .Rcache files.
(recall this is a custom cdf; I have used previous versions of the cdf,
but deleting .Rcache should have gotten rid of that...).

Attached is the plot (black lines should be all of the probes --
subset=NULL -- so it should be the same). Below is the code. I do call
setCdf(), but it shouldn't do anything since it should be the same cdf
that I used to do the normalization with: it's the 'basic' cdf with name
<chiptype>.cdf so it should match the cdf that is used automatically.
(And I have checked with getCdf() and it returns the same pathname).

Best,
Elizabeth

library(affy);
library(aroma.affymetrix);
options(warn=1)#, error=expression(NULL))
chipType<-"hjay"
projectname<-"BRCA,2007,batch1_2"
outdir<-"epurdom/BRCA_2007/Batch1_2" #"BRCA_2007"
cdfHjay<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)
cdfHjayTC<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,tags=c("r1","TC"))
cdfHjayPsrTC<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,tags=c("psr","r1","TC"))
cdfHjayPsr<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,tags=c("psr"))
cdfHjayJuc<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,tags=c("juc"))
psrCells<-getCellIndices(cdfHjayPsr)
jucCells<-getCellIndices(cdfHjayJuc)

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-5)
timestampOn(verbose)
verbose<- -3

myinitials<-"ep"
csBRCAJunct <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name=projectname,
chipType=chipType)

arrayNamesBRCAJunct<-getNames(csBRCAJunct)
batchFac<-rep("2",length(arrayNamesBRCAJunct))
batchFac[grep("Junct",arrayNamesBRCAJunct)]<-"1"
batchFac<-factor(batchFac)
cellLineFactJunct<-sapply(strsplit(arrayNamesBRCAJunct,"_"),.subset,2)
arrayNamesBRCAJunct<-paste(cellLineFactJunct,batchFac,sep="_")
replicates<-names(table(cellLineFactJunct))[table(cellLineFactJunct)>1]

#background correction:
bcBRCAJunct <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(csBRCAJunct,tag=c("*",myinitials))
csBCBRCAJunct <- process(bcBRCAJunct,verbose=verbose)
#quantile normalization:
qnBRCAJunct <- QuantileNormalization(csBCBRCAJunct,
typesToUpdate="pm",tags=c("*",myinitials))
csNBRCAJunct <- process(qnBRCAJunct, verbose=verbose,force=F)

###Here: the density plots
pdf(file.path(outdir,"HjayDensity_normalized.pdf"),width=6,height=6)
setCdf(csNBRCAJunct,cdfHjay)
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset=NULL,col="black")
plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset=unlist(psrCells),col="red",add=TRUE)
plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset= unlist(jucCells),col="blue",add=TRUE)
legend("topright",legend=c("All","PSR probes","JUC
probes"),fill=c("black","red","blue"))
plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset=NULL,col="black")
plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset=unlist(psrCells),col="red")
plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset= unlist(jucCells),col="blue")
dev.off()

this was probably because 'affy' was loaded via an internal require()
after you plotted the raw data.

>
> However, I'm still getting not exactly the same distribution for all the
> quantile normalized arrays when I plot (I've done this for other
> experiments/cdfs and it is *exactly* the same). I have started clean by
> deleting all but the raw cel files and deleting the .Rcache files.
> (recall this is a custom cdf; I have used previous versions of the cdf,
> but deleting .Rcache should have gotten rid of that...).

Yes, cache results from an earlier version of the same CDF could have
been the problem.

>
> Attached is the plot (black lines should be all of the probes --
> subset=NULL -- so it should be the same). Below is the code. I do call
> setCdf(), but it shouldn't do anything since it should be the same cdf
> that I used to do the normalization with: it's the 'basic' cdf with name
> <chiptype>.cdf so it should match the cdf that is used automatically.
> (And I have checked with getCdf() and it returns the same pathname).

> Best,
> Elizabeth
>
> library(affy);
> library(aroma.affymetrix);

> projectname<-"BRCA,2007,batch1_2"
> outdir<-"epurdom/BRCA_2007/Batch1_2" #"BRCA_2007"

> cdfHjayPsrTC<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,tags=c("psr","r1","TC"))
> cdfHjayPsr<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,tags=c("psr"))
> cdfHjayJuc<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,tags=c("juc"))
> psrCells<-getCellIndices(cdfHjayPsr)
> jucCells<-getCellIndices(cdfHjayJuc)
>
> verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-5)
> timestampOn(verbose)
> verbose<- -3
> myinitials<-"ep"
> csBRCAJunct <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name=projectname,
> chipType=chipType)
> arrayNamesBRCAJunct<-getNames(csBRCAJunct)
> batchFac<-rep("2",length(arrayNamesBRCAJunct))
> batchFac[grep("Junct",arrayNamesBRCAJunct)]<-"1"
> batchFac<-factor(batchFac)
> cellLineFactJunct<-sapply(strsplit(arrayNamesBRCAJunct,"_"),.subset,2)
> arrayNamesBRCAJunct<-paste(cellLineFactJunct,batchFac,sep="_")
> replicates<-names(table(cellLineFactJunct))[table(cellLineFactJunct)>1]
> #background correction:
> bcBRCAJunct <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(csBRCAJunct,tag=c("*",myinitials))
> csBCBRCAJunct <- process(bcBRCAJunct,verbose=verbose)
> #quantile normalization:
> qnBRCAJunct <- QuantileNormalization(csBCBRCAJunct,
> typesToUpdate="pm",tags=c("*",myinitials))
> csNBRCAJunct <- process(qnBRCAJunct, verbose=verbose,force=F)
> ###Here: the density plots
> pdf(file.path(outdir,"HjayDensity_normalized.pdf"),width=6,height=6)
> setCdf(csNBRCAJunct,cdfHjay)
> par(mfrow=c(2,2))
> plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset=NULL,col="black")
> plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset=unlist(psrCells),col="red",add=TRUE)
> plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset= unlist(jucCells),col="blue",add=TRUE)
> legend("topright",legend=c("All","PSR probes","JUC
> probes"),fill=c("black","red","blue"))
> plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset=NULL,col="black")
> plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset=unlist(psrCells),col="red")
> plotDensity(csNBRCAJunct,subset= unlist(jucCells),col="blue")
> dev.off()

A few things that might narrow down the problem.

(1) The QuantileNormalization is stratified to be on PMs only (both
fitting and updating). What probes are PMs is defined by the CDF,
that is, what CDF 'csBCBRCAJunct' has when you process() the QN will
make a difference.

(2) It is actually the case that if you do 'typesToUpdate=NULL', the
set of probes processed will still be defined by the CDF, i.e. you
will get all probes in the CDF and if the CDF does not contain all
probes they will also be excluded from the QN.

(3) Try to use QuantileNormalization(..., typesToUpdate=NULL) which at
least outrules the definition on what is a PM.

(4) Do you observe the same for say expression arrays?

See if this helps

Henrik

>>

>>

>>

Hi,

I'm not sure if you narrowed down the problem or not, but I've created
a vignette showing how to stratify by different probe types in
plotDensity() and QuantileNormalization():

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/empirical-probe-signal-densities-and-rank-based-quantile-normalization

I was also bitten by the non-documented/ad hoc default value of
argument 'subset' (=1/2) to plotDensity(). This is something that
was set way back and it was done to speed up the reading/plotting. I
will most likely change this to 'subset=NULL' in the next release.

Have a look at the above vignette and see if it clarifies a few things.

Cheers

Henrik
